newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Jones, Brooke may still play Fiji test.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Jones, Brooke may still play Fiji test.

text.p: WELLINGTON, June 4 - The All Black selectors appear hopeful that loose forward stars Zinzan Brooke and Michael Jones may still be available for the one-off rugby test against Fiji on June 14, NZPA reported on Wednesday.

Brooke was last night withdrawn from the All Black trial in Rotorua on Sunday because of suspicions that he was concussed by a collision with ACT halfback George Gregan in last Saturday's Super 12 final.

Concussions result in a three-week stand-down period but All Black coach and convener of selectors John Hart had still not ruled the No 8 out of consideration after a meeting with fellow selectors Ross Cooper and Gordon Hunter last night.
Hart said Brooke had been withdrawn from the trial match but he would still join the teams in Rotorua and undergo further medical tests.
Brooke's place in the shadow test side, the New Zealand Barbarians, will be taken by Otago captain Taine Randell, who moves off the bench. Auckland's Xavier Rush has been added to the reserves.
Rush was the national Under-19 captain last year and is a member of the New Zealand Academy team which thumped the touring Ireland A side last week.
His elevation to the starting 15 looks to be mainly for experience and so that the trial teams do not have to undergo any great alterations.
Jones is due to have a minor elbow operation today but will also be in Rotorua, although he would not have been available for the Sunday match on religious grounds anyway.
Jones' recovery from the surgery will be monitored closely by the All Blacks' medical team before any decision is made on his availability for the Fiji test.
Two late changes have also been made to the New Zealand A trial team, with Canterbury No 8 Steve Surridge out with a groin injury and Andrew Blowers withdrawn from the reserves.
Surridge has been replaced by Wellington's Filo Tiatia, while Blowers, who has just recently recovered from a back injury, is replaced by Auckland's Finau Maka.

Fullback Christian Cullen, who injured his shoulder in the Central Vikings' loss to Fiji on Monday, and halfback Justin Marshall, who hurt his sternum during the Canterbury Crusaders' last Super 12 match, will have their injuries monitored after the teams assemble on Thursday.
The All Black test side to face Fiji at Albany, north of Auckland, will be named on Sunday evening after the trial, with Cooper yesterday warning that the tourists should not be underestimated.
Cooper was on hand to witness Fiji's 19-10 win over the Vikings in Palmerston North and he was impressed by what he saw.
"They're getting fitter and the pattern in the forwards especially is emerging quite strongly," he said.
"They will continue to get better and they are getting better."
Cooper noted Fiji's discipline and control against the Vikings and was in no doubt that they would give the All Blacks a stern tussle in the New Zealanders' first test of the year.
Vikings coach Frank Oliver also warned that the Fijians' brilliant counterattacking ability would make them a handful.
"They've got a lot of pace, while their flat-line defence was very good," Oliver said.
"They're showing on tour that they have the pace to slide out of tackles."
He said the All Blacks would have to ensure they controlled possession because Fiji could be lethal even with a limited amount of ball.
"They more exposure they get to football here, because they come from so many different unions, the better they will get. And Brad (Johnstone, the Fiji coach) knows what he is doing."
